standard_prerequisites: the rotation group acting on the sphere
the representative set C selecting one member per equivalence class of the orbit relation
composition and inverses of rotations staying in the group
core_obligations: Prove that if two rotations differ then their images of C are disjoint
proof_roadmap: Suppose a point s lies in both images: s is rho1 of r1 and rho2 of r2 with r1, r2 in C
Then r2 is the image of r1 under the composite rho2-inverse after rho1, which is again a group rotation, so r1 and r2 are equivalent under the orbit relation
C picks exactly one representative per class, so r1 = r2; the two rotations then agree on r1, and since both are in C's orbit setup the rotations are equal, contradicting distinctness
difficulty_reason: A short group-action argument; each step (composite in the group, one representative per class) is written out, with the final uniqueness of the rotation on a point doing the last work.
